summary: The paper revisits the Amarasinghe and Lam communication-set algorithms and removes iteration variables that do not affect which element or processor is involved. On an LU kernel this reduces generated communication and cuts running time on a small cluster.
why_read: It is a short, concrete example of how the messages a compiler generates can be pruned by projecting away iteration variables.
main_contribution: Revised communication-set formulas with redundant-iteration projection, implemented as modified code generation algorithms.
main_limitation: Only one LU kernel at one size was measured on a small Fast Ethernet cluster, and examples that need all iteration variables gain nothing.
evaluation_method: measured running time of generated LU kernel on an 8-node cluster, before and after the optimization
states_relationship_to: Shan Shan Wang array data-flow analysis
Ya Nan Shen (automatic code generation of data decomposition)
